_source: C1 finalized from speller close-up photo (2026-07-17): tile rows are the 24 lowercase letters, then final sigma + 3 single accents + 2 breathings + 1 combo, then 5 more breathing+accent combos + the 3 iota-subscript composites. Inventory = 25 letters + 11 marks + 3 composites (39 tiles). All six breathing+accent combinations exist (incl. rough+grave and smooth+grave). On-screen arrangement is the app's own; this inventory is the contract. Diacritic 'apply' = combining sequence appended to the previous character, then NFC-normalize.
_extension_5d: 5D Phase 0 (divergence log D-15, layout A chosen by Nathanael): one added bottom row of punctuation keys + a space bar. The original on-screen keyboard has neither, and the chapter-3 Scripture Memory Spelling Exercise types a 14-word verse; chapter 6's Spell Greek Phrase needs the space too. Punctuation covers the Scripture Memory family through chapter 8 (comma, raised dot, period) plus the Greek question mark. NO CAPITALS and no shift layer: the checking policy folds case under both 'With Accents' settings instead. The question-mark tile inserts U+003B, which is what U+037E normalizes to under NFC. This file is the SHARED contract for every spell surface app-wide; SpellActivity reads it in preference to any inline activity.spellerTiles copy so a chapter cannot fork the keyboard.
_extension_5e3: APOSTROPHE tile added (divergence log D-29, Nathanael 2026-08-07). Chapter 2 TEACHES elision by name -- Learn Marks has an 'Apostrophe' topic deriving dia + autou -> di' autou, the Marking Recognition Drill scores 'Apostrophe' as an answer distinct from 'Smooth Breathing' and 'Coronis', and the Quick Review marks chart lists "Apostrophe: ( ' ) elided letters". Chapter 4's Scripture Memory Spelling Exercise then requires the learner to type di' in John 14:6b, and until this round no tile could produce it. THE MARK IS U+0027 EVERYWHERE -- the key prints it, the key inserts it, and every rendered elision in the data is stored as it. The ORIGINAL had no apostrophe key and wrote elision as a smooth breathing on the preceding vowel; the port does not imitate that. A smooth breathing is a DIACRITIC on a vowel, an apostrophe is a SPACING character standing for a dropped letter, and as of 2026-08-07 the checker accepts neither for the other (Nathanael): answer has an apostrophe, only an apostrophe passes; answer has a breathing, only that breathing passes. U+1FBD and the curled quotes still fold to U+0027 because they are alternate ENCODINGS of the same spacing mark, which is not the same thing as a leniency. The mark is also REQUIRED where a verse elides -- omitting it is a misspelling, unlike sentence punctuation (D-18) -- because it stands for a letter. The key is printed with U+0027, the only apostrophe form with no curl, so it cannot be mistaken for the breathing, the acute or the grave.
